Dr. Cash $20,000; Cr. Accounts Receivable $19,600, Cr. Sales Discounts Forfeited $400
Dr. Cash $20,000; Cr. Accounts Receivable $20,000
Dr. Cash $19,600, Dr. Sales Discounts $400; Cr. Accounts Receivable $20,000
Dr. Cash $20,000; Cr. Sales Revenue $20,000
Under the net method, AR was recorded at $19,600; when the discount expires, the extra $400 collected is credited to Sales Discounts Forfeited (Other Revenue).

A company factors $150,000 of Accounts Receivable without recourse to a finance company. The factor charges a 4% factoring fee and retains 6% to cover potential sales returns. How much Cash does the company receive immediately, and what is the Loss on Sale of Receivables / Service Charge Expense?
Cash $135,000; Loss/Service Charge Expense $6,000
Cash $144,000; Loss/Service Charge Expense $6,000
Cash $135,000; Loss/Service Charge Expense $15,000
Cash $141,000; Loss/Service Charge Expense $9,000
Fee (expense) = $150,000 × 4% = $6,000. Holdback (Due from Factor receivable) = $150,000 × 6% = $9,000. Immediate Cash = $150,000 - $6,000 - $9,000 = $135,000.

To report receivables on the balance sheet at their Cash (Net) Realizable Value and match estimated credit losses to the period of sale
To report receivables at gross face value regardless of collectibility
